title: Trace correctness and recovery through an NLP runtime
description: Switch scenarios to see how representation compatibility, bounded queues, fallbacks, and outcome monitoring protect different parts of the product contract.

nodes.label: Product client
nodes.detail: Sends text with identity, task, locale, priority, and a deadline. It needs an explicit answer, abstention, rejection, or job identity.

nodes.label: Admission gateway
nodes.detail: Authenticates, validates format, estimates tokens, applies tenant and priority limits, and rejects work that cannot meet the contract.

nodes.label: Representation service
nodes.detail: Applies normalization, language routing, tokenization, truncation or chunking, and emits the representation version with every request.

nodes.label: Token scheduler
nodes.detail: Groups compatible requests under token and sequence limits while bounding queue age and honoring cancellation.

nodes.label: Model runtime
nodes.detail: Executes the compatible model, precision, and runtime profile. It returns scores or tokens with timing, stop reason, and artifact version.

nodes.label: Validated fallback
nodes.detail: A smaller model or deterministic policy preserves a narrower, pre-evaluated contract when the primary path cannot finish.

nodes.label: Decision policy
nodes.detail: Validates schema, calibrates or aggregates model output, applies safety and business rules, and chooses return, abstain, or escalation.

nodes.label: Quality telemetry
nodes.detail: Joins privacy-safe request cohorts, bundle versions, system signals, decisions, and delayed outcomes to detect slice-specific regressions.

scenarios.label: Healthy request
scenarios.summary: A bounded request carries one compatible representation and model bundle through a token-aware queue, then records both system and decision evidence.
scenarios.result: The caller receives a decision before its deadline, and operators can join that result to the exact tokenizer, model, policy, latency, and later outcome.

scenarios.label: Tokenizer mismatch
scenarios.summary: A model rollout expects a new vocabulary, but one representation replica still emits the previous token IDs. The process is healthy while the semantic contract is broken.
scenarios.result: Fail compatibility checks and stop the bundle rollout. Retrying the same mismatched path cannot restore correctness; the tokenizer and model must deploy as one compatible unit.

scenarios.label: Queue overload
scenarios.summary: A burst of long inputs consumes the scheduled-token budget. Waiting for the primary runtime would exceed the caller deadline.
scenarios.result: The scheduler caps queue age and routes eligible work to a pre-evaluated smaller model. Other work is rejected or deferred explicitly instead of timing out after consuming more capacity.

scenarios.label: Slice quality drift
scenarios.summary: Latency and error rates remain healthy, but delayed outcomes show a quality drop for long Arabic documents after a representation change.
scenarios.result: System health alone would miss the regression. Slice-aware outcome monitoring blocks further promotion and triggers rollback of the representation-model-policy bundle.
